sentences.text: Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm rather than the mitochondrion.
sentences.quote: Glycolysis is in the cytoplasm, not the mitochondrion.

sentences.text: During this process, glucose is divided into two molecules of pyruvate.
sentences.quote: Glucose is split into two pyruvate molecules.

sentences.text: The first half of the process consumes two ATP, while the second half produces four ATP.
sentences.quote: Two ATP are spent in the first half and four are made in the second half.

sentences.text: Additionally, two NAD+ are reduced to NADH during glycolysis.
sentences.quote: Along the way, two NAD+ are reduced to NADH.

sentences.text: This results in a net gain of 2 ATP for each glucose molecule.
sentences.quote: Net gain from glycolysis: 2 ATP per glucose.
